aoi.title: Area of interest
aoi.description: Pick the area to monitor. It is saved with the project and every download is cut to it.
aoi.info_md:
Pick the area this project monitors: an administrative area, a polygon you draw, or an Earth Engine asset. It is saved with the project as soon as you select it, and every download is cut to it.

- The **coverage** of every alert source over this area is checked once and saved in the project; the Alerts step shows it.
- Once the project has an alert set, the AOI is locked: a new area would invalidate every download and every footprint. Use **Duplicate** in the Project dialog to monitor another area with the same sources, masks, layers and grid.
aoi.locked: This project already has alert sets, so its AOI is locked. Duplicate the project (Project dialog) to monitor another area.
aoi.no_geometry: The AOI has no usable geometry; select it again in the AOI step.

alerts.title: Alert sources
alerts.description: The alert datasets this project monitors, with the share of the AOI each one covers. Each is downloaded for every period, cut to the AOI and the period's dates.
alerts.info_md:
An alert source is a dataset of forest-loss alerts. Each alert pixel is **confirmed** (high confidence) or **probable** (low confidence) and carries the day it was first detected.

- **Predefined:** GLAD-L (Landsat, about 30 m), GLAD-S2 (Sentinel-2, 10 m) and RADD (Sentinel-1, 10 m). RADD detects only in primary humid tropical forest; elsewhere in its area it reports no alerts.
- **Custom:** an Earth Engine image or image collection, or a GeoTIFF in your SEPAL folder, read through a format preset: *RADD* (alert band 2 probable, 3 confirmed; date `yyddd`), *SEPAL CCDC alerts* (1–2 detections probable, 3 or more confirmed; first detection date in decimal years) or *date only* (one date band in the encoding you choose; every dated pixel is confirmed).

The chip on each row is the source's **coverage**: the share of the AOI inside its footprint. A source that covers none of the AOI cannot be added; a partial coverage is a warning. A project holds at most 3 predefined and 6 custom sources. A custom source can be edited until an alert set uses it; after that, delete it and add a new one.

layers.title: Optional layers
layers.description: Layers that help you read the alerts: an Earth Engine image, a GeoTIFF from your SEPAL folder, or Planet NICFI. They can also be shown on the two Analysis maps.
layers.info_md:
Visualization layers help you read the map; they never change the alerts.

- **Earth Engine image:** one band drawn with a palette, or three bands as an RGB composite, between a minimum and a maximum.
- **GeoTIFF** in your SEPAL folder: one band drawn with a colour map. The app writes an overview file next to it, so its folder must be writable.
- **Planet NICFI:** the monthly tropical mosaic through Earth Engine, for the month you choose or the last month of the active period. Your Earth Engine account needs NICFI access.

Show a layer on this map with its row's map button; its legend appears with it. Tick **Show in Analysis** to add it, switched off, to both Analysis maps.

period.title: Periods
period.description: Each period downloads every source over its dates plus the look-back days before them. Pixels already reported by the sets of earlier periods are skipped, so a late-published alert lands in the next period's set and no pixel is reported twice.
period.info_md:
A period is one monitoring round, usually a month. For each period every source is downloaded over its **search window**: the period's dates plus the **look-back** days before them, so that alerts published late are still found.

- Pixels already reported by the alert sets of earlier periods are removed before vectorizing, so a pixel is never reported twice.
- **New period** starts the day after the latest period and copies that period's mask choices.
- A period's dates cannot change once it has alert sets. A period can be deleted when it has no sets, or when it is the latest period; its downloads and files are deleted with it.
- Select a row to make it the active period of Download & harmonize and Integrate & vectorize.

prepare.title: Download & harmonize
prepare.description: Download every mask and source of the active period in its own projection, then align them onto the project grid and apply the period's masks (harmonize). Nothing whose inputs are unchanged runs twice.
prepare.info_md:
This step prepares every input of the active period on the project **grid**: one projection in metres and one pixel size.

1. **Grid:** an EPSG code (the target button suggests the UTM zone of the AOI) and a resolution. It is locked once the project has an alert set.
2. **Masks:** rasters defined once per project (an Earth Engine image or a GeoTIFF, one band; a pixel is on where its value is not zero). Each period chooses which masks are on and whether each **keeps** its area (alerts outside it are removed) or **excludes** it (alerts inside it are removed). A mask is downloaded once and aligned to the grid.
3. **Sources:** each source is downloaded over the period's search window in its own projection, then aligned to the grid and masked (harmonized).

Nothing whose inputs are unchanged runs twice: a new grid or a mask switch only harmonizes again, without downloading. **Run all** runs the masks first, then every source that is missing or out of date, and skips the rows that read *Not covered* or *No data for this period*. Each row needs twice its compressed size free on disk.

integrate.title: Integrate & vectorize
integrate.description: Combine the downloaded sources, skip pixels an earlier period already reported, and turn the clusters into alerts.
integrate.info_md:
This step turns the harmonized sources of the active period into an **alert set**: the alerts Analysis reviews.

1. The chosen sources are combined pixel by pixel; each alert remembers which sources detected it.
2. Pixels already reported by the sets of earlier periods (their **footprint**) are removed.
3. Neighbouring pixels become alerts. Alerts smaller than the **minimum size** are dropped; you can keep only a drawn area and limit the number of alerts, sorted as you choose.
4. An optional **attribute raster** (Earth Engine or GeoTIFF) adds a statistic of its bands to every alert.

An alert set is identified by its period and sources: running the same combination again **replaces** it, after a confirmation that lists the reviewed alerts it would discard. When the run ends, Analysis opens on the new set.
